# Released native desktop observations

[Meeting recording and desktop ownership](meeting-owner-evidence.md) adds fourteen joined released recorder/HTTP/archive transactions and nine actual application Meeting workflows/47 GTK states. The real native owner now binds MeetingPage to capture/preferences, with owned background finalization, retained retry, selective locks, diagnostics, cancellation and shutdown. The root application and full Meeting acceptance remain Pending.

[Earlier Meeting records, retry and archive page](meeting-evidence.md) adds compatible private JSON/audio archival, fifteen actual diarized HTTP workflows and six real Meeting pages/44 GTK states. Failed index writes, explicit retry, privacy erasure, real exports/title edits and deletion dialogs match their bounded released observations. A further native in-flight Incognito-drop fault leaves no audio or index. Complete application lifecycle remains pending.

These synthetic fixtures compare native GTK components with unchanged Mluva 1.6.0 at commit `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. The temporary reference collectors run outside the maintained Rust tree, import only the frozen downloaded release, and check imported files byte-for-byte against that commit. `desktop-reference.json` records the source and bundled-font digests. The desktop CSS, semantic palettes, capability labels and four JetBrains Mono faces preserve released assets; the font's OFL license is included. Capability labels describe the released application and do not claim acceptance of the entire Rust replacement.

[Provider/setup/workspace evidence](provider-pages-evidence.md) freezes 47 actual released transactions/290 GTK states and 243 local-language/alias decisions. The explicit private check uses real catalog/keyring boundaries, save/reopen failures, selected-generation download conflicts and additional native parent-refresh/page-exit guards. It preserves the sole authorized reduction to three local slider identities. Successful page-driven downloads, full parent assembly and visual/modal/scale acceptance remain open.

[Capture preferences and settings ownership](capture-preferences-evidence.md) adds seventeen unchanged-release transactions/132 GTK/store states, actual config/profile failures, native metadata processes, mode/style/language/key/privacy controls, shared prompt editing/recovery and settings/setup navigation. All twenty-two released maturity rows match. An extra native unwritable-audio-route fault now returns with saved choices after repair of reentrant model replacement; the nonterminal reference and initial native crash remain documented. Whole application/provider/Meeting/review lifecycle and desktop acceptance stay pending.

`theme-cases.json` contains six exact stylesheet outputs and seven valid/invalid synthetic Omarchy palette observations. The native desktop test also exercises actual scheme changes, palette reload/removal and controller cleanup in its own private data directory.

`document-widget-cases.json` records 14 source/revision pairs in reading, editing, revision and reading-after-revision states, for 56 observations. Each captures actual GTK buffer source and visible text, tag intervals, Pango document heights at three widths, wrapping, formatting limits, tooltip text and insertion/selection marks. It records the reference widget digest, GTK 4.22.4, Pango 1.58.2 and scale 1. Renderer changes require collecting new observations from the same unchanged release. Both implementations currently emit the same Pango cursor warning on mixed CR/LF input; the observations still match. Neither warnings nor complete document workflows are declared resolved by this fixture.

`personalization-desktop-evidence.json` summarizes paired off-screen component runs at scale 1. The released and native surfaces ran sequentially in one disposable X11/session-bus/accessibility environment. External AT-SPI actions filled fields and activated buttons; a guarded native XTest helper expanded rows only on the private display. The initial page and saved dictionary, snippet and style states were compared for exact pixels and accessibility roles, names and actions. Saved documents were compared after generated UUID normalization, with 0600 file modes. Raw screenshots, logs, settings and desktop metadata remain private under the worktree's ignored `tmp/` directory.

`prompt-editor-cases.json` records 71 observations from ten actual released GTK editor flows, plus ten observations from the released application's own prompt-session guard. They cover exact text and whitespace, counts, button states, close/discard confirmation, Save/reopen/restore, UTF-8 repair, control/length validation, external file conflicts, Incognito viewing and a privacy change immediately before Save. File bytes, permissions and change/close notifications are observed through native widgets and the filesystem. The session guard preserves the first draft when another prompt is requested and permits a new edit after closing it. GTK 4.22.4, Pango 1.58.2 and Libadwaita 1.9.3 are recorded; the native test refuses changed versions until observations are renewed from the unchanged release.

`prompt-editor-desktop-evidence.json` summarizes ten external-input comparisons of the shared catalog, editor, confirmation, conflict, restore and saved-style preview. Both surfaces use the same synthetic paths sequentially within one private session. The reference comparison binds the unchanged application's actual editor/open/change methods without constructing providers or capture services. Motion and cursor blinking are disabled equally, and the pointer is parked outside the private application before capture. All accessibility role/name/action observations and saved results match; nine states match RGBA8 bytes exactly. The initial catalog differs by one channel unit on 16 pixels in the standard maximize icon, at the recorded bounds. This difference is retained explicitly; no exact-pixel or animation claim is made for that state. Saving style instructions changes only the local prompt override, preserves the original personalization JSON and creates no History item.

`application-shell-cases.json` records eight preference-navigation observations, 30 command-catalog observations and 25 search/dialog observations from released code. Each catalog contains 51 command identities and checks live availability after document identity, actual editor identity, capture phase, privacy, pane and processing changes. The dialog flows exercise Unicode casefold/whitespace search, unavailable actions, keyboard wrapping, dismissal and a state change between selection and final dispatch. Preference deep links expand the original nested rows and focus them. Native tests inspect ordinary public GTK widgets; no production test hooks expose the implementation's internal state.

`root-window-cases.json` records 36 observations from the released application's actual window construction and navigation, retaining its own command and prompt-opening methods. Native counterparts exercise 1060/737/736/735/420 widths, adaptive controls, page titles, utility buttons, modal shortcut guards, hide/reopen, commands requested while hidden and shared prompt opening. All 13 action names/types match; two external `gdbus` calls deliver the same typed arguments on separate connections to the private session bus. This proves the action publisher, not the remaining review-policy, capture, overlay or delivery services.

`application-shell-desktop-evidence.json` binds the 102 matching observations to the frozen source digests and native source/lockfile digests. Eight window snapshots are compared as decoded RGBA8: four match exactly, while four differ at 3–23 pixels by at most two channel units. Bounds and hashes retain these differences explicitly. Motion and cursor blinking are disabled equally. Capture, welcome, meeting, history and Workspace/Capture preference contents use synthetic boundaries; Prompts and Personalization are real production components in both windows. Raw captures and logs remain private under ignored `tmp/`.

`settings-command-binding.json` adds three released observations of a deferred settings command after its original row is removed during refresh. The command retains its destination, selects the original preference page and preserves the original row binding. This case failed against the initial weak binding and passes with the same bounded ownership as the release; commands are not attached to the original widgets, so the retained binding introduces no widget cycle.

`text-target-cases.json` freezes thirty real accessibility-transport cases against a separate native GTK Entry/TextView/PasswordEntry process. A fresh client's first case captures an already-focused field; further cases compare actual Unicode edits, selections/carets, current-focus keyboard guards, explicit Command reads, password exclusion, tracker close, disabled/absent services and process exit. Twenty-nine readiness-gated private bus monitors independently observe zero text reads outside four explicit Command selection ranges. Embedded-NUL insertion failed before its C-string prefix repair. The [target evidence](text-target-evidence.md) records source/fixture digests, native ownership, isolated application/cache setup and exact remaining boundaries. This fourth ignored GTK test was explicitly executed; it proves the target layer rather than the complete paste/capture controller or browser/Wayland insertion.

`firefox-target-cases.json` adds 21 real-browser target/delivery cases against Firefox 154.0/build 20260818182641. Cold capture, UTF-16 edits, real xclip/xdotool paste, stale/late/own focus, password/read-only/refused fields, NUL clipboard recovery, rich text and Command limits match the release through an independent DOM/event observer. Twenty-one readiness-gated monitors include three positive Command reads; the supported no-P2P debug setting makes those bus observations visible. The [browser evidence](firefox-target-evidence.md) records exact transport scope, corrected startup, process cleanup and the private network/PID/device runner. This fifth ignored GTK test was explicitly executed. Peer/monitor support is shared with the original thirty-case GTK test; native production code is unchanged in this browser milestone.

The [conversation workspace evidence](conversation-page-evidence.md) adds 86 actual page actions and 27 frame-clock scrolling states through the production workspace and compatible SQLite stores. It covers unsaved documents/prompts, explicit saves and failed-save recovery, history/titles/pagination, a positively confirmed database merge, private/transient results, prompt overrides, live Questions/panes, screenshot owners and volatile previews. The empty persisted-title control failed before repair. Fourteen fence cases, twenty XML decisions, thirty-six forecast samples and sixteen lossless Questions splits have independent released outputs; Unicode separator splits failed before repair. Six actual offline WebKit/native-texture states match source, notices, dimensions and all five rendered PNG hashes. The final isolated run also repeats the existing 56 document-widget observations after whole-document sizing changed. See the evidence for exact digests, private runner and remaining boundaries.

The [capture/control evidence](capture-controls-evidence.md) adds 38 actual model/thinking-menu states and 40 capture/recovery states. The native capture page embeds the production workspace, rewrite settings, recording dock and unresolved-output editor. Hidden/stale model choices, reasoning/Fast support, provider changes, returned shortcut hints, Live cycles/rejections, callouts and review callbacks match the release. The final owner also repeats all 113 conversation/scroll states. Recording, saving, provider discovery and review services are explicit callback boundaries; this is widget evidence, not an asynchronous capture-controller or microphone proof.

The [capture transaction evidence](capture-lifecycle-evidence.md) joins the production controller/session, asynchronous audio owner, real loopback batch/realtime clients and compatible History. Seventeen independently released transactions match 81 GTK states, complete results, audio retention and exact PCM uploads. They cover preparation, Escape, repeated stop, frozen rules, Incognito, committed-only realtime and explicit batch fallbacks. Two further native faults check Incognito Notes cleanup and controller exit during a real pending HTTP request, including no late clipboard write. Exact fixture/source digests, the title/Escape failures before repair, responsive timers and remaining service boundaries are recorded in the evidence.

The [Live evidence](live-evidence.md) adds sixteen actual released Live transactions/68 states and ten joined captures/54 states, through actual rewrite/speech transports and production GTK controllers. It checks revisions, final coalescing, frozen prompts/configuration, Once, durable replies and save-failure recovery, paused/partial copy policy and continuation root/full-source ownership. The final owner passes all 26 transactions/122 states and repeats the existing 46 capture transactions/218 states plus three native faults. Independent core fixtures add 320 scheduling transitions and 61 prompt decisions.

The [document/review evidence](review-evidence.md) adds 29 actual released transactions/102 GTK states through the native rewrite factory, real Codex children, editable workspace and compatible stores. Streamed previews remain volatile, revision/privacy/deletion/cancellation guards preserve the original, and frozen image bytes survive deletion before model dispatch. Deliberate Copy/dismiss/open/continue/preset/style actions and typed widget projections match. An additional native exit fault verifies exact child reaping and no late reply/clipboard/review write. Seventy-eight independent projection cases and ten actual private-bus receipts preserve both status signals, replay and erasure; no host bus is used.

The examples and window test provide comparison surfaces around production widgets; they are not the complete Mluva application. Complete welcome/settings/capture flows, full Live/Grilling/compatible/local/review integration, animation timing, other sizes/scales, remaining error states, full provider/service assembly and application accessibility are still pending in the [acceptance matrix](../../../../docs/rust-port-parity.md). Native tests read static fixtures without an interpreter. Follow [the native workspace instructions](../../../README.md) to build the private input example and run GUI checks inside the private helper; never run input probes on the host display or concurrently against an automatically selected Xvfb display.
